title: Lake Minnow Rising
premise: Ulyana Coldharbour has spent seventeen years in Lake Minnow keeping their head down, counting the days until graduation frees them from a town that pretends they don't exist. When a group chat called Minnow Rising starts posting predictions that come true with eerie precision, Ulyana realizes the messages are coming from someone who knows what the school board buried decades ago: the disappearance of a student in 1987, erased from every record. As the predictions turn darker and point toward a repeat of the past, Ulyana and three unlikely allies dig into the town's sealed archives, discovering the missing student was queer and silenced by the very families who still run the school. In the climax, Ulyana exposes the truth at the centennial assembly as the final prediction comes due, forcing the town to choose between its comfortable lies and its forgotten child—and choosing, at last, to remember.
about_author: Sable Eriksen grew up in a small lakeside town where everyone knew everyone's business except their own, an experience that taught them how silence can shape a person. They write young adult stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes in their own hometowns.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Strangers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine day at Lake Minnow High establishes their invisibility: misgendered at roll call, ignored in the halls, dreaming of a college two thousand miles away. The emotional beat is weary resignation—Ulyana has made peace with being a ghost, until a strange text arrives from a number they don't know: 'Day 1. It starts with you.'

chapters.title: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They discover four classmates received the same message and were added to a chat called Minnow Rising: golden-boy Marcus, conspiracy-obsessed Priya, quiet farm kid Dev, and Ulyana's former best friend turned stranger, June. The first prediction—that the gym roof will leak during Friday's pep rally—comes true exactly. Beat: uneasy curiosity overriding distrust.

chapters.title: Predictions Come Due
chapters.summary: Rotating POV among the five teens. More predictions land: a teacher's resignation, a car crash on Route 9, each accurate to the detail. The school board announces an emergency meeting about 'digital misinformation.' Beat: the thrill of secret knowledge curdling into fear—they're not receiving prophecies, they're receiving warnings.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Print
chapters.summary: June's POV. Researching old yearbooks for clues, June finds a 1987 photo where one face has been carefully inked out, and a class list with nine hundred names but no record of a transfer out. She confides in Ulyana, their first real conversation since middle school. Beat: fragile reconnection; the past has a hole shaped like a person.

chapters.title: The Sealed Wing
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev reveals his grandfather was the school custodian in '87 and left him a key to the records room the district claims flooded and was demolished. Inside: a box labeled COLDHARBOUR—Ulyana's own family name. Beat: dread and vertigo; this isn't just history, it's inheritance.

chapters.title: Danny Coldharbour
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The box holds letters from Danny Coldharbour, Ulyana's great-aunt's sibling—a queer student who vanished in 1987 after the principal threatened to out them. The last letter predicts their own disappearance. Ulyana realizes the chat's voice matches Danny's writing. Beat: grief and fury; the town didn't lose Danny, it erased them.

chapters.title: Warnings Turn Personal
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The predictions shift: naming the five teens, then dates—June's date is three days after graduation. Marcus, whose father sits on the school board, finds his dad shredding documents and must decide where his loyalty lies. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve; staying invisible is no longer survivable.

chapters.title: The Board's Buried Boys
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The five go public with Danny's letters online, and the town splits—some families confess long-held guilt, others threaten lawsuits and worse. The board cancels graduation. Priya traces the chat's origin to the records room's old intercom system, still live. Beat: rising stakes; the enemy isn't supernatural, it's institutional.

chapters.title: Centennial Assembly
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. At the town's centennial assembly, Ulyana takes the stage uninvited and reads Danny's final letter aloud as the board tries to cut the microphones. The crowd's phones light up with the chat's last prediction: 'Day 100. Say my name.' Nine hundred voices answer. Beat: cathartic defiance; visibility as victory.

chapters.title: Lake Minnow Rising
chapters.summary: June's POV, resolution. Weeks later: an independent investigation opens, Danny's name goes on the memorial wall, and the five friends plant a garden where the records room stood. Ulyana still counts days until graduation—but now they're counting toward something. Final beat: belonging found not by escaping home, but by making it tell the truth.
